name: API, data or compute seller
oneLine: Wants per-request or metered payment with no accounts and low fees.
goals: Charge per request or per unit of usage with no sign-up, API key or invoice.
Get paid before or at the moment the response is served, with no chargeback exposure.
Serve humans and agents from one endpoint: 402 for payers, 200 for everyone who paid.
Keep fees low enough that sub-cent prices still make sense.
Be discoverable by agents through a bazaar, a directory or an OpenAPI extension.
Support metered sessions for streaming or long tasks without one settlement per chunk.
pains: Facilitator fees and chain fees set a floor under the smallest viable price.
x402 and MPP both serve the pay-per-call case; some clients speak only x402 and others prefer MPP (whose mppx client can also pay x402 exact offers), so serving both reaches the most clients.
Reported transaction counts are inflated by leaderboard farming and memecoin activity, so real demand is hard to read.
A payment that settles after the resource was served can fail, and the seller has already given the data away.
Compliance is unclear: receiving stablecoins from unknown wallets raises sanctions screening and tax questions the seller cannot answer alone.
Clients retry with replayed or expired signatures, and each verify call to the facilitator costs time.
decisions: Which protocols and rails to accept, and in which order to list them in accepts[].
Which payment flow to use: authorization (verify, serve, settle), upfront, or escrow.
Which facilitator to use, and whether to run one.
Price per request versus a session or subscription, and the deposit size for sessions.
Whether to require identity (Web Bot Auth, an ERC-8004 agentId) in addition to payment.
